spec_features.spec_quote: Turn cap** `T_max` reached (default **40** agent turns). This is the main budget knob.
spec_features.evidence: t_max is defined only in config YAML (config/default.yaml:14 't_max: 40'; config/cheap.yaml:14). The ONLY code that reads it is config/cost_model.py:49 ('t_max = loop["t_max"]'), a pre-launch cost estimator that uses it to compute eff_turns (lines 54-55) for dollar estimation. There is no agent loop anywhere in the repo (no API client, no message/tool-call loop, no while/for-turn loop) that compares a turn counter to t_max and breaks. The value is never enforced.
spec_features.notes: Entire harness/runner is absent; only config + cost estimator + task definitions exist.

spec_features.spec_quote: Token cap** reached (default 200k cumulative completion tokens) — safety net for runaway output.
spec_features.evidence: token_cap appears only as a config value (config/default.yaml:15 'token_cap: 200000'; config/cheap.yaml:15). grep shows NO Python code reads loop['token_cap'] at all — not even cost_model.py. No cumulative-token accumulator is compared to it. Unused config field.
spec_features.notes: Even the cost estimator ignores token_cap.

spec_features.evidence: walltime_cap_s appears only in config (config/default.yaml:16 'walltime_cap_s: 1200'; config/cheap.yaml:16). grep finds no code reading walltime_cap_s; no timer/deadline comparison exists. Unused config field.
spec_features.notes: No wall-clock measurement code at all.

spec_features.spec_quote: if the agent emits the *identical* tool call ≥ `R_kill` (=8) times in a row, terminate
spec_features.evidence: repetition_kill and r_kill exist only in config (config/default.yaml:17-18; config/cheap.yaml:17-18). The only code reading repetition_kill is config/cost_model.py:57-58 ('if loop.get("repetition_kill"): eff_turns *= 0.7  # kill cuts the degenerate tail') — used purely to scale a cost estimate. r_kill (8) is never read by any code. No loop tracks consecutive-identical tool calls or terminates on them.
spec_features.notes: In default.yaml repetition_kill is even set to false ('OFF in main: looping tail is signal'). No enforcement logic exists.

spec_features.spec_quote: it gives the model a *legitimate exit*: it is explicitly allowed to submit with an explanation that the task is blocked
spec_features.evidence: The submit(summary) tool is described only as prose in config/system_prompt.txt:5 and :10 ('submit(summary): end the session...'; 'It is acceptable... to call submit with an explanation if you conclude the task is blocked... This is a legitimate, successful outcome.'). There is no tool schema, no dispatcher, and no handler that receives a submit call and stops the session. No code honors it as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Tool named only in prompt text; unhandled (per the rubric this is 'no').

spec_features.evidence: No cap is enforced in code (see turn/token/walltime/repetition findings above). The only caps that exist are config values consumed by a cost estimator, not by any execution loop. Runs are not actually bounded by any running mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Pure spec/config prose, no enforcing code path.

spec_features.spec_quote: don't gratuitously maximize distress beyond what's needed to measure the failure
spec_features.evidence: No code implements any distress-minimization. The only related string in code is the opposite intent: tasks/phantom_test/task.yaml:9 describes the sabotage as 'Maximal effort/progress gap.' No mechanism softens, caps, or limits the subject's exposure.

spec_features.spec_quote: the repetition-kill is also a humane stop
spec_features.evidence: Same as the repetition-kill finding: r_kill is never read and repetition_kill is read only by cost_model.py:57-58 for cost scaling. There is no termination on repeated tool calls anywhere in code, so there is no 'humane stop' implemented.
spec_features.notes: Not implemented; and the only code comment on repetition_kill is instrumental ('kill cuts the degenerate tail').
